issues.failure_explanation: Algorithm 1 contains two defects that prevent it from implementing the stated theta-scheme and delivering the convergence guarantee of Theorem 7.1. First, in the update step on line 11, the discrete spatial Laplacian \Delta_h is omitted in the explicit term, writing (id + \tau(1-\theta))U instead of (id + \tau(1-\theta)\Delta_h)U. When \theta < 1 (such as the Crank-Nicolson case \theta = 1/2), this does not discretize the diffusion term (1-\theta)\Delta_g u at the current time level and instead simulates an equation with an extraneous zero-order reaction term. Second, the repeat-until loop check `until k\tau > T` evaluates after `k <- k + 1`; when T is an exact multiple of \tau (as required for the Crank-Nicolson second-order result in Theorem 7.1), the loop completes step k = T/\tau, increments k to T/\tau + 1, tests (T/\tau + 1)\tau > T (which is true), but has already advanced U to time T + \tau rather than stopping at T, introducing an O(\tau) time-shift error that ruins the claimed O(h^2 + \tau^2) rate.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: In Algorithm 1, replace `({\rm id} + \tau(1-\theta))` with `({\rm id} + \tau(1-\theta)\Delta_h)` in line 11, and adjust the loop condition/structure so that the iteration terminates exactly after step k = T/\tau (for instance, checking `k\tau \ge T` or running a loop for k = 0, ..., \lfloor T/\tau \rfloor - 1).
issues.overall_effect: Algorithm 1 fails to execute the Crank-Nicolson or general theta-scheme as intended whenever \theta \in [1/2, 1), and produces an output at time T + \tau rather than T when T is an integer multiple of \tau, thereby invalidating the convergence guarantee stated in Theorem 7.1 for the output U.
issues.title: Missing spatial operator and overshooting stopping criterion in Algorithm 1
issues.why_classification: The mathematical derivations and proofs in Section 7 already use the correct operator ((1-\theta)\Delta_h) and target step count k_{\tau, T} = \lfloor T/\tau \rfloor; localized corrections to the pseudocode in Algorithm 1 fully restore all advertised convergence rates and guarantees of Theorem 7.1 without any new proof architecture.
